risk.risk_capacity_notes: Stated tolerance -30% (~57k SEK at current size). REVISED 2026-07-07: the goal is softer than previously recorded (see horizon) — not a hard deadline. That eases the original glidepath tension (a -30% drawdown in year 6 is less catastrophic if the purchase can slip), but vagueness cuts both ways: an uncommitted goal can also crystallize EARLIER or the money be wanted for something else. Treat the glidepath re-anchor trigger (goal becomes concrete) as the operative control, not the calendar.

horizon.primary_goal: Property purchase, nature UNCERTAIN (user statement 2026-07-07): 'not completely sure what I am saving for' — most likely an apartment or similar. One live idea: a Mediterranean vacation apartment, rented out when not used, while renting in Sweden (rental income offsetting Swedish rent). Explicitly vague, not set in stone, a potential long-term goal.
horizon.years_until_needed: 3-7 (SOFT — goal not committed; treat as flexible, not a hard deadline)
horizon.currency_note: If the Mediterranean option materializes, the future liability is EUR, not SEK — this reverses the standing rationale for tilting the equity sleeve toward SEK/Nordic. Flag for the Council whenever the goal firms up.

buffer.notes: Standard buffer confirmed 2026-07-04 — the portfolio's risk budget is genuine, not partly an emergency fund.

cash_flow.recurring_foreign_currency_inflow: ~750-1000 EUR roughly every 2 months, irregular occasions, landing in PayPal (disclosed 2026-07-12). Not salary - described as money that 'comes in at different occasions'.
cash_flow.fx_note: PRIORITY: repeated small FX conversions through PayPal's native conversion are a structural fee-drag risk (PayPal's spread is typically well above mid-market - CONFIRM actual rate, do not assume) that compounds every ~2 months indefinitely. This is a lever #2-class problem (fee drag) even though the sums are small, because it recurs forever. See portfolio.json open_structural_questions 6 for the routing options to evaluate. Do not let 'the amounts are small' excuse ignoring this - it's the recurring nature, not the size of one instance, that makes it structural.

reference_targets.note: v1-amended, ADOPTED by Council ruling 2026-07-07 (same-day amendment to reports/2026-07-07-council-memo.md) - transcribed here 2026-07-12 after discovering it was decided but never written back to this file, a process gap in its own right. Anchor: today treated as T-5 (midpoint of the 3-7y SOFT range in `horizon`); re-anchor trigger is the goal firming up, not the calendar. Equity reverted to 50% (from an initially proposed 45%) because the goal lost its hard deadline: with `horizon.years_until_needed` now soft, the recoverability constraint that justified 45% no longer binds, and 50% sits at the stated -30% drawdown tolerance with zero slack - not beyond it. The 20% SEK/Nordic currency tilt originally proposed alongside 45% was DROPPED (liability currency now unknown - could be SEK or EUR per `horizon.currency_note` - so currency matching is void in both directions; plain global unhedged equity is the neutral stance).

deposit_year.note: equity is a ceiling (<=10%), cash is a floor (>=50%)

reference_targets.PENDING_RECONCILIATION: 2026-07-12: user has separately proposed a RISK-TIER framework (70% secure/non-volatile, 20% medium risk, 10% high risk actively traded weekly/daily) - see risk_tier_framework_proposed below. This is a materially different decomposition (risk-tier, not exposure-class) and the two have NOT been reconciled. Do not silently merge them - next Council sweep must adjudicate.

risk_tier_framework_proposed.status: PROPOSED by user 2026-07-12, NOT YET ADOPTED - needs Council reconciliation against reference_targets above before either is treated as authoritative.
risk_tier_framework_proposed.user_description: User wants investments explicitly split into risk-categorized tiers: ~70% secure and non-volatile, ~20% medium risk, ~10% high risk. The high-risk tier is intended to be actively worked - user wants to try to grow it on a weekly or even daily basis.
system_flags_for_council: The 10% high-risk/active-trading tier lines up almost exactly with CLAUDE.md's existing short-horizon rule (Short <6mo: tactical overlay ONLY, capped at 10% of portfolio, never High confidence, always flagged tactical) - this is a point IN FAVOR of the proposal fitting the system's existing guardrails, not a new risk. Council should say so explicitly rather than treating it as a fresh debate.

The 70% 'secure' figure is MORE conservative than the currently adopted glidepath's 45% fixed_income+cash (40+5) at the 'now' column - a straight read implies either the risk-tier framework should replace the exposure-class glidepath's starting point, or 'secure' is being defined more broadly than fixed_income+cash (e.g. including part of the equity sleeve if it's low-volatility/index vs the high-risk tier being carved OUT of the existing crypto+tactical allocation rather than added on top). Definitional mapping is unresolved - Council must define which existing holdings/exposure-classes map to which risk tier before producing SEK numbers.
Does not override reference_targets.glidepath_table by default - both are recorded as of 2026-07-12; whichever framework wins (or how they're merged) is a Council decision, not assumed here.
